fields.h1: Build a Bathroom Sign in Sheet for Passes and Cleaning Checks
fields.hero_description: Build a bathroom sign in sheet that logs student passes or restroom cleaning checks, with the time saved on each entry.
fields.features_heading: What a Paper Restroom Log Leaves Out
fields.features_subheading: A clipboard by the door records a name and a time. The sheet Emergent builds knows who is out and which check is late.
fields.feature_1:
One student out per pass

When a student taps out, the sheet marks the pass as in use until they tap back in. The next student sees who has it and when they left, so nobody asks the teacher mid-lesson.
fields.feature_2:
A QR code on each door

Print the sheet's link as a QR code and post it on the door. Staff and visitors open it on their own phones, with no app to install and no clipboard on a nail to go missing.
fields.feature_3:
Cleaning tasks with initials

Each check lists the jobs for that room, such as soap refilled and floor mopped. The attendant ticks each one and adds initials, and the sheet records the time it was saved.
fields.feature_4:
A message when a check runs late

Set the check times once. If a check is 15 minutes past due with no entry, the app emails the shift lead or posts in Slack, naming the restroom and the check that was missed.
fields.feature_5:
Every entry in a database you own

Each pass and each check is a row in a database you own, with the name, the room, and the times. Filter by week or by student to see a pattern without retyping a paper log.
fields.feature_6:
Your sheet's code in GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A district IT team can host it on its own servers, connect it to other tools by API and keep changing it by prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Signs the Sheet, and Who Reads It
fields.tab_content_1:
Yusra waits for Tobiah to tap back in

Wren Hollis teaches 7th grade science in Room 214 at Bayside Middle School, and her class shares one restroom pass on a tablet by the door. Tobiah taps out at 10:12 AM. When Yusra taps at 10:15 AM, the sheet shows the pass in use and who has it. She sits back down, and the pass is hers once Tobiah taps back in.
fields.tab_content_2:
Ondine signs off after 6 of 6 tasks

Attendants at Dunmore Fuel check the customer restroom every 2 hours while the store is open. At the 2:00 PM check, Ondine Farrow scans the code on the door and ticks 6 tasks: toilets, sinks, soap, paper towels, floor, and trash. She adds her initials, and the sheet saves the check with the time she finished.
fields.tab_content_3:
Clogged toilet posted in Slack, fixed by noon

Patrons at Ashcombe Library report problems from the code on each restroom door. At 11:20 AM, someone in the 2nd floor restroom picks Clogged toilet from a list. The report posts to the facilities channel in Slack with the room and the time. Custodian Orrin Paget marks it fixed at 11:48 AM.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 6 cafes, one logs under 50 checks

Each of the 6 Briarwood Roasters cafes has restroom checks scheduled 8 times a day, 56 a week. A cafe that logs under 50 of 56 gets flagged. On Monday, district manager Nell Abernathy opens the weekly view. Every other cafe logged at least 52 of 56, and Galloway Junction logged 41 of 56, the one flag on her list.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Bathroom Sign in Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a bathroom sign in sheet that records each pass or cleaning check with its time, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the log you are keeping
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep pass entries to two taps
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide how many can be out
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write tasks the way staff say them
fields.howto_step_1_des: A classroom pass log and a restroom cleaning log share a name and little else. One tracks people leaving a room, the other tracks work done in one. Decide which you need before writing a single field, because the fields differ.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Load the class roster so students pick their name instead of typing it. The sheet stamps the time out on the first tap and the time back on the second. Add a destination only if students also leave for the nurse or office.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set the number of students allowed out of one room at the same time. A class that shares a single pass sets it to one. Tell students the rule on the first day, and the waiting message on the tablet will make sense to them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List each cleaning task as a short phrase an attendant can tick in a second: soap refilled, trash emptied, floor mopped. Keep the list short enough to read on one phone screen, and each task becomes its own column in the log.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set check times and a contact
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose the times each restroom is checked during open hours. Name the person who gets a message when a check is late, and pick email or Slack. Leave a missed check as a gap in the log rather than filling it in later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Post the link where people use it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Mount the door code on the inside of each restroom door at eye level, where staff see it while they work. For a classroom, keep the sheet open on a spare tablet near the exit. Scan each code from two phones before day one.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Describe it, then test a week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Tell Emergent what the sheet logs and who gets each message. It builds the form and the database behind it, including any rule you named. Run one week of real entries, then change anything that slowed people down by describing the change.

faq_plan.q: What is a bathroom sign in sheet?
faq_plan.a: A bathroom sign in sheet is a log of who used or serviced a restroom, and when. Classrooms keep one for student passes, with a name, a time out, and a time back. Businesses keep one as a cleaning record, with the check time, the tasks done, and the initials of whoever did them.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a bathroom sign in sheet?
faq_plan.a: Decide whether it logs passes or cleaning checks, then list the fields: a name and two times for passes, or tasks and initials for cleaning. Describe that, plus any rule such as one student out at a time, to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the sheet, the database behind it, and the views you asked for.

faq_plan.q: What columns does a bathroom sign in sheet need?
faq_plan.a: It depends on which log you keep. A pass sheet needs the student's name, the time out, and the time back, plus a destination if students also visit the nurse. A cleaning sheet needs the date, the check time, one column per task, and the initials of the person who did the work.

faq_plan.q: Should a bathroom sign in sheet be separate from other classroom sign-ups?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A restroom pass changes every few minutes and needs a time on each entry, while a club sign up sheet collects names once and stays the same for weeks. Keeping them apart leaves the pass log short enough to read at a glance during a lesson.

faq_plan.q: How often should staff fill in a bathroom sign in sheet for cleaning?
faq_plan.a: Match it to traffic. A busy fuel stop or cafe might check every 2 hours while open, and a small office might check twice a day. Put the check times on the sheet in advance. A missed check then shows as an empty slot instead of a line nobody remembered to add.

faq_plan.q: Can a bathroom sign in sheet limit how many students are out at once?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the sheet tracks the pass instead of only listing names. You set the number allowed out of one room, and it can differ by class period, such as two during a long lab. When the limit is reached, the next student sees who is out and waits.

faq_plan.q: Is a free bathroom sign in sheet template enough for a classroom?
faq_plan.a: For one pass and no rules, a blank template on a clipboard works. It falls short once you want to see who has the pass right now, or count trips by week. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a live version. The same builder makes other shared lists, such as a potluck sign up sheet.

faq_plan.q: How do I get staff to use a bathroom sign in sheet on every check?
faq_plan.a: Make logging faster than skipping it. Put the code where the work ends, on the door on the way out, and list only tasks the attendant does anyway. Go over the weekly log with the team, gaps included, and ask about each missed check while the shift is still fresh in mind.

faq_plan.q: Can a bathroom sign in sheet show patterns over a semester?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once entries are rows instead of handwriting. The sheet Emergent builds saves each pass to a database you own, class period included. Count trips by student or by week. Treat a pattern as a reason to talk with the student, never as a verdict on its own.

faq_plan.q: Who should initial a bathroom sign in sheet after cleaning?
faq_plan.a: Whoever did the cleaning, with their own initials, at the moment they finish. One shared login, or one person signing for a whole shift, hides who checked what. Fire drills and safety trainings belong on a separate safety sign in sheet, which records attendance rather than tasks.
